decision: prefetch window design: the viewability handler (on_viewable_items_change) widens the report's viewable pair by LOOKBACK=50 / LOOKAHEAD=250 rows, clamped to the listing; inside ONE stored borrow it fills the model's ListWindow - keeping rows the window already holds, reading the missing ones in ascending index order via the seam's track_row - then wants a THUMB cover for every row it read, ascending. No signal is written in the handler; rows repaint through the cells' own rebinds, covers through the pump's revision bump
why: P0 correction 22 makes the direct per-row read pattern miss the budget (scattered ~10.6 ms/call); ascending reads keep the projection's 8x50-row FIFO page cache sequential (the span of lookback+lookahead ~6 windows never thrashes it); correction 24 puts the cover ask ahead of the viewport because cold decode is the limiter
result: built; the headless request-order test reads the covers mock's log ascending and bounded

decision: row bindings read the ListWindow (O(1), no store read); a miss falls back to the seam's own track_row inside the binding (the first frame before the first report, a jump faster than the report). The bindings read state.list_revision (a pump bump on every window reset) beside the window, so a committed Library mutation repaints the visible rows from the refilled window
why: correction 12: the index is read INSIDE bindings (a copy would freeze the cell); correction 21: reading a signal is what re-runs a binding - the window cache alone is not reactive
result: headless: rows render from the mock; the selection survives recycling

decision: eviction policy (the View half): CoverViews in model.rs - the LRU-by-insert cap is COVER_VIEWS_CAP=200 entries (the egui COVER_CACHE_CAP carried over) AND a 64 MB RGBA byte budget (the egui COVER_TEXTURE_BYTE_BUDGET), both enforced on insert; evicted keys are reported to CoverCache::forget so a re-ask re-requests; the order carries each entry's byte cost, and no read mutates the order (a render binding's read stays read-only)
why: P0 corrections 10 and 24: nsh's image cache has no numeric bound, so the policy must live on the nsh side; the entry cap binds first for thumbs (12.5 KB each ~ 2.5 MB at 200), the budget is the heroes' guard (N9's 512 box is 1 MB)
evidence: crates/riff-gui-nsh/src/model.rs CoverViews + unit tests (cap, re-arrival, byte budget)
result: unit tests hold both bounds and report the drops
